task.title: The desktop window cannot be dragged on macOS
task.description:
On macOS the Workbench window has no region a user can grab to move it. main.js opens the window with titleBarStyle 'hiddenInset', which removes the native title bar, so the only draggable area is whatever the renderer marks with -webkit-app-region: drag. styles.css marks .sidebar-head that way only for other platforms (:root:not(.is-mac) .sidebar-head { -webkit-app-region: drag }); the macOS head gets a 34px top inset to clear the traffic lights and no drag region at all. This has been so since the shell's first commit (e7bc0af, 2026-09-04); the Windows build drags by the same head, which shows the WebContentsView honors the property. Found by Dylan on the first notarized build, desktop-v0.6.0-rc4, and it blocks v0.6.0.

Fix: make .sidebar-head the drag region on every platform, keeping the macOS inset, in both the expanded sidebar and the collapsed 76px rail, with every control inside it (the chevron, any button) opting out via no-drag so a click still clicks. Pin it with a stylesheet check in the desktop tests. Verify by hand in a packaged or dev run on a Mac: the window moves when dragged by the sidebar head in both layouts, the chevron still toggles the rail, and the traffic lights still work. The board area is a separate WebContentsView owned by the Go board page, so it stays non-draggable; a drag strip across the top of the board would be a follow-up if the sidebar head is too small a target.
